title: Effect of pore geometry on ultra-densified hydrogen in microporous carbons
material_description: TE7 | phenolic-resin-based activated carbon beads (MAST Carbon International), carbonised phenolic resin activated in CO2 at 1173 K; disordered pore structure (randomly ordered graphitic layers); PSD maxima 0.7 and 1.2 nm
activation_method: CO2 activation at 1173 K (by the manufacturer, as described in the paper)
source_location: main file, page image main-09 (journal p. 976), Fig. 9a, series TE7 (filled red triangles)
notes: archive: fig9a_TE7_filled_triangles_adsorption.json; pressure digitized in MPa and multiplied by 10 to bar; Fig. 9a run: different pressures and point count from the Fig. 9b/S7 run of the same sample, so a separate run; filled = adsorption, open = desorption by the paper's Fig. 3 convention; open triangles and ~8 filled triangles hidden near p = 0 not extracted (see log.md); isotherm_point_count is a lower bound of markers counted; Fig. 9a x axis has no title, taken as MPa as in panels c-d; Table 2: BET 1234 ± 7 m2 g-1, total pore volume 1.33 cm3 g-1 (P/P0 = 0.95), micropore volume 0.42 cm3 g-1, PSD maxima 0.7, 1.2 nm (0.7 stored). TGA: > 97 wt% carbon.; H2: Hiden Isochema HTP-1 Sieverts-type volumetric analyser, 77 K (liquid-nitrogen bath), H2 99.99996% (Air Products BIP-Plus); ~100 mg samples degassed ex situ at 473 K for 10 h under dynamic high vacuum (~10^-4 Pa) (printed: 473 K, 10 h, ~10^-4 Pa; ~100 mg); free-volume determination not described; 'repeat isotherms for different samples were reproducible to within 0.3% of measured amounts absorbed' (relative, so uncertainty_wt_pct left empty). basis_evidence: Fig. 9 caption: '(a) Experimental excess H2 sorption isotherm at 77 K for TiC-CDC-800, SWCNTs, and TE7 carbons. activation_method: CO2 flow (100 mL min-1) at 673 K for 40 min to remove end caps before use
source_location: main file, page image main-09 (journal p. 976), Fig. 9a, series SWCNTs (open blue circles)
notes: archive: fig9a_SWCNTs_open_circles_desorption.json; pressure digitized in MPa and multiplied by 10 to bar; open circles = desorption by the paper's Fig. 3 convention (Fig. 9 caption does not define the open symbols; methods: adsorption/desorption measurements, isotherms fully reversible); marker centre taken at each circle's centre dot; adsorption branch of this run (filled circles) digitized from Fig. 9d; Fig. 9a x axis has no title, taken as MPa; Table 2: BET 945 ± 5 m2 g-1, total pore volume 0.89 cm3 g-1 (P/P0 = 0.95), micropore volume 0.38 cm3 g-1, PSD maxima 0.7, 1.0, 1.2 nm (0.7 stored). BET measured on the CO2-treated tubes. TGA: > 97 wt% carbon.; H2: Hiden Isochema HTP-1 Sieverts-type volumetric analyser, 77 K (liquid-nitrogen bath), H2 99.99996% (Air Products BIP-Plus); ~100 mg samples degassed ex situ at 473 K for 10 h under dynamic high vacuum (~10^-4 Pa) (printed: 473 K, 10 h, ~10^-4 Pa; ~100 mg); free-volume determination not described; 'repeat isotherms for different samples were reproducible to within 0.3% of measured amounts absorbed' (relative, so uncertainty_wt_pct left empty). Laboratory not stated; corresponding author (M. Tian, first marked) used. N2 77 K, Micromeritics 3Flex, outgassed 473 K 8 h; BET ranges chosen by Rouquerol consistency criteria (range not printed); PSD by 2D-NLDFT; total pore volume at P/P0 = 0.95; micropore-volume method not stated.
basis_evidence: Fig. 9 caption: '(a) Experimental excess H2 sorption isotherm at 77 K for TiC-CDC-800, SWCNTs, and TE7 carbons. Experimental excess H2 uptake as a function of pressure and modelling at 77 K for (b) TE7, (c) TiC-CDC-800, and (d) SWCNTs. ... the solid red lines are the fitted isotherms, and the blue dashed lines represent the calculated absolute uptake.' Text p. 975: 'the experimental Gibbs excess isotherms for H2 adsorbed at 77 K were modelled ... and then converted to absolute H2 uptake (Fig. 9b-d)'. SI Eq. S1: m_E = 100(rho_A - (1/Z)(PM/RT)) theta_A v_P.
